question: A conversion in the Core Renewal Area will add 24 homes to a building that has been vacant for six consecutive years. The primary structure will be retained, and 5 units will be restricted for 30 years to households earning no more than 50% of AMI. Does this satisfy the required affordability obligation, and can the project pursue expedited review and the retrofit grant?
policy_text: Section 1 — Covered conversions: A conversion of a vacant nonresidential building to residential use in the Core Renewal Area is covered if it adds at least 15 dwelling units. Section 2 — Obligation for projects adding 15 to 29 units: The developer must either provide 2 units affordable to households earning no more than 60% of area median income (AMI), with restrictions lasting at least 20 years, or pay the applicable fee. These options may not be combined. Section 3 — Enhanced conversion option: A covered conversion that restricts at least 20% of its units to households earning no more than 50% of AMI, for 30 years, satisfies the Section 2 unit obligation and is eligible for expedited permit review. Section 4 — Retrofit grant: A conversion may apply for a structural-retrofit grant if it adds at least 20 homes, the building was vacant for at least five consecutive years before conversion, the primary structure is retained, and it meets the enhanced option in Section 3.
project_path: Proceed through the covered-conversion permit route, record 30-year restrictions on the 5 units at or below 50% AMI, and seek expedited permit review. The project may also submit an application for the structural-retrofit grant.
reasoning_steps: The conversion is in the Core Renewal Area and adds 24 homes, meeting the location and minimum-unit conditions for coverage.
Because the project adds between 15 and 29 units, it must provide 2 units at or below 60% AMI for at least 20 years or pay the fee.
Five of 24 units is more than 20%; those units meet the stricter 50% AMI limit and carry 30-year restrictions, so the enhanced option satisfies the unit obligation.
The enhanced option makes the project eligible for expedited permit review.
The project adds at least 20 homes, the building was vacant for six consecutive years, the primary structure is retained, and the enhanced option is met; therefore it may apply for the grant.
supporting_clauses: Section 1 covers conversions in the Core Renewal Area adding at least 15 units. Section 2 sets the obligation for projects adding 15 to 29 units. Section 3 states that a 20% set-aside at or below 50% AMI for 30 years satisfies that obligation and qualifies for expedited review. Section 4 lists the grant conditions, all of which are met by the project facts in the question.
eligibility_conclusion: The conversion is covered and satisfies its affordability obligation through the enhanced option. It is eligible for expedited review and meets all stated conditions to apply for the structural-retrofit grant.
